transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Nguyen (Redwood SE), Jesse Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Zenith Partnerships), Daniel Moore (Zenith Cloud Integrations), Lena Ortiz (Zenith Security)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on Redwood marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for a joint solution (Zenith marketplace + Redwood Private option), and security/compliance questions (KMS, SOC2 scope, audit logs). Focus on timeline for listing and a follow-up private deployment deep dive.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing assets: screenshots, tile copy, pricing options
- Reference architecture: network flow, VPC peering vs private link, auth & routing
- Private deployment considerations: capacity, autoscaling, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Security review items: SSO, RBAC, data residency, logging retention
- Next steps and who owns assets for marketplace submission

Transcript:
[15:00] Sofia Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. um quick roll call?
[15:02] Priya Rao: Priya here from Zenith, Daniel and Lena are with me. thanks Sofia.
[15:03] Daniel Moore: yup Daniel here.
[15:04] Lena Ortiz: Lena, security architect.
[15:05] Sofia Patel: great. so agenda is marketplace listing + ref arch + security questions. Marco from our se team will walk through technical bits.
[15:06] Marco Nguyen: hey all, i'll share my screen in a sec. so, high level — we typically need a listing tile, short and long descriptions, screenshots of console, container of sample API calls, and a reference arch doc if you want a joint solution badge.
[15:07] Priya Rao: perfect. timeline for listing — we were hoping to go live mid may, is that realistic?
[15:08] Sofia Patel: mid may is tight but doable; depends on assets and compliance checks. if we get your assets this week and Lena can sign off on the security appendix early next week we can queue the listing review.
[15:09] Daniel Moore: when you say assets, is there a template? we want to avoid rework.
[15:10] Marco Nguyen: yes — we'll send a checklist. screenshot sizes, copy length, a sample integration diagram. i'll attach a sample reference-arch we use for AuroraCloud partners; it's mostly the same. note: some of the names in the doc might be out of date — sorry, old r-names.
[15:12] Lena Ortiz: on security, high level questions — do you support customer-managed KMS for private deployments? and what about audit log retention?
[15:13] Jesse Kim: yes for Redwood Private we support customer-managed KMS integrations (KMS or HSM), and audit logs can be forwarded to your logging stack — we typically support 90 days by default but can extend for enterprise. note there are RBAC roles in the control plane.
[15:14] Lena Ortiz: and for the marketplace listing, will any customer data be passed to Redwood hosted control plane? we need clarity for data residency.
[15:15] Marco Nguyen: good question — for the listed marketplace experience, the listing is basically a referral + provisioning workflow. if you choose hosted (Redwood Hosted) then usage flows through our hosted runtime; for Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed and data stays in your VPC. we should call out the options explicitly on the listing.
[15:16] Priya Rao: ok that's helpful. can we also support cost estimation examples on the listing? customers ask for ballpark unit economics.
[15:17] Sofia Patel: yes we can include example pricing scenarios; we'll flag that they're estimates and that dedicated pricing differs. keep in mind Marketplace marketplaces sometimes require a single price field so include a note that final billing happens under Zenith after provisioning.
[15:19] Daniel Moore: on network connectivity, we run with private link and peering across accounts. for private deploy, which do you recommend?
[15:20] Marco Nguyen: PrivateLink tends to be simpler for cross-account secure connectivity; VPC peering can work but gets messy at scale. Redwood Private supports both, our deployment manifest can include a network section. i'll share sample manifests.
[15:22] Lena Ortiz: can you confirm whether KV cache or token caches are stored in ephemeral storage only? any long-lived data?
[15:23] Jesse Kim: by default KV/kv cache is ephemeral in the inference runtime — not persisted beyond instance lifecycle unless you enable an optional cache persistence layer. for marketplace joint solutions we usually recommend ephemeral with prefix/KV caching turned on but no long-term customer content stored.
[15:25] Priya Rao: great. what's needed for the reference architecture diagram — do you want specifics like autoscaling thresholds or just a logical diagram?
[15:26] Marco Nguyen: logical diagram plus a callout for autoscaling knobs (min/max workers), expected concurrency for demo flows, and an example of fallback policy if a model isn't available. if you're including a dedicated offering, show how routing to Redwood Dedicated pools works and fallback to hosted.
[15:28] Daniel Moore: we have 2 main flows: provisioning from marketplace (one-click) and a managed service option for larger customers. can Redwood support both?
[15:29] Sofia Patel: yes both are supported. the one-click uses our provisioning API and can optionally create a Private deployment profile in customer's cloud. the managed service option would be a Reserved Dedicated contract — needs sales/legal alignment.
[15:31] Lena Ortiz: compliance items — SSO/SAML, SCIM, and single tenant control plane?
[15:32] Marco Nguyen: SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning identities supported on the control plane. single-tenant control plane is part of a Private on-prem or VPC deployment; that's in enterprise offering. we'll include an architecture note on that.
[15:34] Priya Rao: about the marketplace acceptance checklist — are there common gotchas? we want to avoid rejection after submission.
[15:35] Jesse Kim: common ones: screenshots missing helmet (i meant correct console screenshots), pricing mismatch between tile and details, missing security appendices, and not including an integration test no. also sometimes the sample API keys included are live ones — don't do that.
[15:36] Daniel Moore: haha noted.
[15:37] Sofia Patel: we'll send a validated checklist. Marco, can you also include a short runnable terraform snippet for the provisioning step?
[15:38] Marco Nguyen: yes i can. sample terraform + post-provision webhook for Zenith. i'll add comments about required iam roles.
[15:40] Priya Rao: for listing copy, can Redwood draft the short description and we'll iterate?
[15:41] Sofia Patel: yes we'll draft an initial tile and description and send it for approval.
[15:43] Lena Ortiz: one last security question — if customers choose Redwood Hosted via the marketplace, can they bring their own encryption keys?
[15:44] Jesse Kim: hosted currently supports CMK rotation for enterprise customers with dedicated tenancy; otherwise we recommend Private for strict BYOK requirements. we can surface an enterprise note on the listing.
[15:46] Daniel Moore: ok sounds good. any required legal contacts for marketplace contracts?
[15:47] Sofia Patel: there's a marketplace vendor team we'll loop in; i'll include legal contacts in the email thread when we share the checklist.
[15:49] Priya Rao: thanks. recapping next steps?
[15:50] Sofia Patel: recap: Sofia send checklist + sample assets by 4/29; Marco send deployment manifest and terraform snippet by 5/3; Zenith provide reference-arch diagram and SOC2 scope by 5/5; schedule security deep dive (private deploy) week of 5/4.
[15:51] Priya Rao: yep we'll aim for those dates.
[15:52] Sofia Patel: perfect, thanks all. we'll follow up in email with links to the sample docs and a calendar invite for the security deep dive.

Notes/References:
- Link to Redwood marketplace sample assets (sent after call)
- Sample reference architecture (attached in follow up)
- Terraform snippet placeholder: /s/repo/marketplace-provisioning/terraform

End of transcript.
